findings.title: A name-only edit while the folder is away turns the deferred color upgrade into a forced write over another Mac's color
findings.body:
`upgradeDefaultColor` caches `color = "kaipu"` on this Mac only (line 448). Now suppose the folder is away and the user renames the workspace. `edit` keeps `color = before.color`, which is that cached `kaipu` (lines 576, 625), deletes `pendingColorUpgrade` (line 629) and sets `pendingIdentity` (line 631). When the folder comes back, the `pendingIdentity` branch writes `color: entry.color` over whatever is in the file (lines 666-671). If another Mac recoloured the Default to, say, sky in the meantime, that change is replaced with kaipu, with no message. The user never picked kaipu; only the deferred upgrade did. This breaks the promise in the docstring at line 427 ("A name or color the user already changed … on another Mac, is left as it is"), which the new yield path at line 681 exists to keep.

A possible fix: when the edit does not patch the color, keep `pendingColorUpgrade` next to `pendingIdentity`. In the `pendingIdentity` branch, write the cached color only if `isOldDefault`-style checks show the file's color is still rose; otherwise keep the file's color. The test at `registry-create-edit.test.ts:206` covers only the case where the folder did not change, so it would still pass.

findings.title: The deferred-upgrade write uses an identity read before an await, with no lock against a concurrent edit's folder write
findings.body: `availability` reads the file (line 657), checks `pendingColorUpgrade` and `isOldDefault` (line 681), then writes `{ ...identity.identity, color }` (line 684). Nothing serializes `availability` against `edit`'s `writeIdentity` (line 612): `UPDATE_LOCK` covers only the prefs write. Consider a probe that passed line 681 but whose atomic write lands after an edit's write. The probe writes back the old name, and the edit's `update` has already cleared `pendingIdentity`. The next probe then takes the folder's file as the truth (lines 693-707), and the rename is lost. The `pendingIdentity` branch at line 666 already has the same window. A per-workspace lock around the folder writes in `availability` and `edit` would close both.

thread_replies.reply: Confirmed: the rollback now calls `removeIdentity` when there was no file before (lines 638-640).
Confirmed: the name is checked again inside the locked `update` (line 621), and `NameTakenError` maps to `name-taken`.
Confirmed: `refusalMessage` takes `editing` and uses `editNotWritable` / `editFailed`.
Thanks. Resolving the late answer inside `act` makes the test catch a missing `alive` guard.

The main case is fixed: a `pendingInit` workspace now accepts a moved folder that has `.kaipu/` items and no identity (line 848), and a test covers it. The second case is still refused: the moved folder already holds an identity with an id this Mac doesn't know, for example another Mac migrated the same drive. Lines 836-838 return `different`, but `availability` would adopt that id (line 711). The `pendingInit && !this.get(identity.id)` rule isn't applied in `checkRelocate` yet.

This push doesn't change `relocateActive`. The new early return in `relocate.ts` skips the transaction only when the same folder is picked. A real move of the active workspace still calls `dropPendingCaptures()`.

Confirmed: `relocateWorkspace` now returns the unchanged entry when the picked folder resolves to the current path (relocate.ts:42-43), and `relocate.test.ts` checks that nothing in the transaction runs.
Confirmed: the “Move to” / «Mover a» sentence is gone from both locales, and the test now asserts it is absent.
Confirmed: the dialog and the context both catch a rejected relocate and show `relocateUncertain`. Wording it as "can't tell" instead of "failed" is better than what I suggested.
Confirmed: the test now runs a relocate, checks that Save stays disabled, then changes the color and checks that Save becomes enabled.

input.summary: This push adds a separate `pendingColorUpgrade` marker so the deferred brand-color upgrade gives way when another Mac changed the folder. It also lets a `pendingInit` workspace be repointed at a moved folder that has no identity, returns early when the same folder is picked, and handles rejected create/edit/relocate calls with \"can't tell\" messages in en and es. It addresses most of the earlier threads.\n\nOne gap remains in the upgrade work. If the user renames the workspace while its folder is away, the cached kaipu color is written over a color another Mac set in the meantime (fix, medium). A second, lower-confidence race: probe writes and edit writes to the folder's file are not serialized. Still-open threads: `checkRelocate` refuses a `pendingInit` workspace whose moved folder holds an identity this Mac doesn't know (another id), and relocating the active workspace still drops pending captures.

This breaks the promise in the docstring at line 427 ("A name or color the user already changed … on another Mac, is left as it is"), which the new yield path at line 681 exists to keep.

A possible fix: when the edit does not patch the color, keep `pendingColorUpgrade` next to `pendingIdentity`. In the `pendingIdentity` branch, write the cached color only if `isOldDefault`-style checks show the file's color is still rose; otherwise keep the file's color. The test at `registry-create-edit.test.ts:206` covers only the case where the folder did not change, so it would still pass.

findings.title: The deferred-upgrade write uses an identity read before an await, with no lock against a concurrent edit's folder write
findings.body: `availability` reads the file (line 657), checks `pendingColorUpgrade` and `isOldDefault` (line 681), then writes `{ ...identity.identity, color }` (line 684). Nothing serializes `availability` against `edit`'s `writeIdentity` (line 612): `UPDATE_LOCK` covers only the prefs write. Consider a probe that passed line 681 but whose atomic write lands after an edit's write. The probe writes back the old name, and the edit's `update` has already cleared `pendingIdentity`. The next probe then takes the folder's file as the truth (lines 693-707), and the rename is lost. The `pendingIdentity` branch at line 666 already has the same window. A per-workspace lock around the folder writes in `availability` and `edit` would close both.

thread_replies.reply: Confirmed: the rollback now calls `removeIdentity` when there was no file before (lines 638-640).
Confirmed: the name is checked again inside the locked `update` (line 621), and `NameTakenError` maps to `name-taken`.
Confirmed: `refusalMessage` takes `editing` and uses `editNotWritable` / `editFailed`.
Thanks. Resolving the late answer inside `act` makes the test catch a missing `alive` guard.

The main case is fixed: a `pendingInit` workspace now accepts a moved folder that has `.kaipu/` items and no identity (line 848), and a test covers it. The second case is still refused: the moved folder already holds an identity with an id this Mac doesn't know, for example another Mac migrated the same drive. Lines 836-838 return `different`, but `availability` would adopt that id (line 711). The `pendingInit && !this.get(identity.id)` rule isn't applied in `checkRelocate` yet.

This push doesn't change `relocateActive`. The new early return in `relocate.ts` skips the transaction only when the same folder is picked. A real move of the active workspace still calls `dropPendingCaptures()`.

Confirmed: `relocateWorkspace` now returns the unchanged entry when the picked folder resolves to the current path (relocate.ts:42-43), and `relocate.test.ts` checks that nothing in the transaction runs.
Confirmed: the “Move to” / «Mover a» sentence is gone from both locales, and the test now asserts it is absent.
Confirmed: the dialog and the context both catch a rejected relocate and show `relocateUncertain`. Wording it as "can't tell" instead of "failed" is better than what I suggested.

structured_output.summary: This push adds a separate `pendingColorUpgrade` marker so the deferred brand-color upgrade gives way when another Mac changed the folder. It also lets a `pendingInit` workspace be repointed at a moved folder that has no identity, returns early when the same folder is picked, and handles rejected create/edit/relocate calls with \"can't tell\" messages in en and es. It addresses most of the earlier threads.\n\nOne gap remains in the upgrade work. If the user renames the workspace while its folder is away, the cached kaipu color is written over a color another Mac set in the meantime (fix, medium). A second, lower-confidence race: probe writes and edit writes to the folder's file are not serialized. Still-open threads: `checkRelocate` refuses a `pendingInit` workspace whose moved folder holds an identity this Mac doesn't know (another id), and relocating the active workspace still drops pending captures.
